Set up Salesforce sign-in

Source: R/backend__salesforce.R
oauth_db_salesforce_client.Rd

Set up Salesforce sign-in for a Shiny app that queries CRM records, Data Cloud or both. Pass the client to shinyOAuth's UI and server modules. Visitors sign in with their own Salesforce account and keep their existing data permissions.

Usage

oauth_db_salesforce_client(
  client_id,
  redirect_uri,
  client_secret,
  ...,
  login_url = "https://login.salesforce.com",
  data_cloud = FALSE,
  provider = shinyOAuth::oauth_provider_oidc_discover(.odb_salesforce_origin(login_url)),
  scopes = c("openid", "profile", "api", "refresh_token", if (data_cloud)
    "cdp_query_api")
)

Arguments

client_id

Application ID from the OAuth registration.

redirect_uri

Registered URL where the browser returns after sign-in.

client_secret

Client secret from the Salesforce registration. Pass NULL only with a custom public-client provider matching that registration.

...

Other arguments for shinyOAuth::oauth_client().

login_url

Salesforce login origin: your My Domain URL, "https://login.salesforce.com", or "https://test.salesforce.com".

data_cloud

Include the cdp_query_api consent scope.

provider

Custom shinyOAuth provider, replacing OIDC discovery.

scopes

OAuth scopes, replacing the defaults.

Value

A shinyOAuth OAuthClient. Create it outside server().

Details

Register an External Client App with the authorization-code flow and PKCE, which protects the sign-in code. Enable JWT-based access tokens for named users; this format works with shinyOAuth's token validation. The default client discovers sign-in settings from login_url over HTTPS.

shinyOAuth manages token renewal. If Salesforce omits the token's expiry, shinyOAuth warns and uses its configured fallback lifetime. Your app's registration and users still need the relevant API and data permissions.

See also

oauth_db_salesforce_api(), oauth_db_salesforce_data_cloud_api(). vignette("salesforce", package = "shinyOAuthDB") has registration steps and a complete app.
